proposal.hypothesis: A watch-time auxiliary head trained only on legal train feedback will regularize embeddings toward consumption intensity and produce complementary within-user ordering beyond the current engagement-MTL parent, improving portfolio marginal contribution even if standalone gain is small.
proposal.implementation_plan: Edit target, train, and predict blocks to replace delegated SO target/train usage with a visible custom PyTorch trainer that keeps long_view as the main binary objective while adding one auxiliary watch-time regression head. In target: use DV.watch_ratio() train-only to build a legal watch-time target such as log1p(clipped_ratio)/12 with validity mask, plus an incomplete/completed censor flag derived from ratio and valid; call DV.assert_trainable on all train-only tensors. In train: build a small embedding-based MTL model over the existing categorical X matrices returned by build_features, with one sigmoid main head for long_view and one scalar watch head; optimize BCE(main) + aux_weight * censored regression loss where incomplete plays use squared error to transformed watch target and completed plays use one-sided lower-bound hinge against transformed duration proxy from watched ratio saturation. Keep fixed train-only checkpoint policy and no candidate-visible early stopping. In predict: output only the main long_view score. Leave inference features unchanged and use no exposure-after-feedback columns.
proposal.justification: This is a materially new reward design relative to the parent: consumption-time supervision rather than only binary engagement auxiliaries. E003 is directly applicable as a mechanism pattern and explicitly warns not to replace the label. Because existing portfolio members are highly correlated within user (w001 vs w002 rank correlation 0.8928231594133691; w002 vs w003 0.8327371603950816), a differently supervised member may add useful residual diversity.
proposal.observation: E003 reports: "Keep native long_view as the ranking objective and add a small censored watch-time regression head sharing FM embeddings... BPR plus this auxiliary target at weight 0.2 reached five-seed official-validation primary 0.604023290 ± 0.000282947 versus 0.603517127 ± 0.000631158 for BPR alone." The current parent already uses multi-task engagement auxiliaries with hp aux_weight=0.2, and the search directive prioritizes portfolio residual exploit. Also train_target_phi_with_long_view shows weak-to-moderate relation for several engagement targets, while long_view remains the official label.

research_evidence.query: How should watch time complement native long_view without changing evaluation labels?
research_evidence.reason: The native binary label discards engagement magnitude and completed plays are right-censored by duration.
research_evidence.summary: Keep native long_view as the ranking objective and add a small censored watch-time regression head sharing FM embeddings. Transform play time and duration with log1p/12. For incomplete plays use exact regression residual; for completed plays use a one-sided lower-bound hinge that stops penalizing predictions above log-duration. Never use evaluation-period feedback as an input feature. BPR plus this auxiliary target at weight 0.2 reached five-seed official-validation primary 0.604023290 ± 0.000282947 versus 0.603517127 ± 0.000631158 for BPR alone; on three random-exposure seeds, unbiased primary was 0.376328528 ± 0.003245064 versus 0.373291085 ± 0.002151737. This is an implementation prior, not permission to replace the fixed relevance label.

selection_rationale:
Candidate 0 is the best next measured experiment because it offers the strongest product of expected marginal portfolio gain, evidential reliability, and implementation reliability. It is a trusted first-round exploit explicitly applicable to the selected parent, edits only the features block, is directly wired to an executable consumer via SO.build_features, and should change feature_dim and predictions if connected. The added hour and strictly-earlier user-gap fields vary at impression level, so they can plausibly improve within-user ordering and refine the existing DeepFM member with low code risk and low cost. In a portfolio-active setting, this kind of safe member refinement with clear connection to inference is preferable to a larger but shakier custom rewrite.

Candidate 1 is also viable and similarly low risk, but it is weaker than Candidate 0 on marginal portfolio priority. The static user-profile fields are legal and connected, yet their incremental value is less convincing because the parent already has user_id embeddings and DeepFM may already capture much of that user-side signal. The candidate itself notes the main risk: static profiles may add little beyond user_id. Since both 0 and 1 are cheap, connected feature augmentations, Candidate 0 has the better expected payoff because temporal/impression-context features directly alter per-impression ranking context, whereas static user attributes are more likely to be redundant with existing user representations. Candidate 1 therefore ranks second.

Candidate 2 has some appeal for portfolio diversification because it changes supervision and could decorrelate rankings, and it has curated research support for the general mechanism. However, it is substantially weaker on implementation reliability for the next measured step: it requires replacing the delegated trainer with a custom PyTorch path across target/train/predict, is much costlier, and has materially higher risk that the custom path underperforms or that the auxiliary mechanism is noisy in this environment. The research evidence is mechanism-level rather than direct evidence on this dataset/stack, and the directive explicitly favors credible connected gains over speculative larger ones. Because portfolio reward still depends on actual executable marginal contribution, Candidate 2 ranks below the two trusted operator-based feature changes for this round.

Overall ranking: 0 > 1 > 2.
